requirement.title: MapleSure Member Sign-In
requirement.description:
# Business Requirement REQ-2026-121 — MapleSure Member Sign-In

**Requested by:** Group Benefits Digital Experience (Business Owner: P. Moreau)
**Date:** 2026-08-17
**Priority:** High
**Type:** New application — no existing system provides this capability

## Business objective

MapleSure members currently have no dedicated online entry point: every
digital journey begins with a phone call to the service desk for identity
verification. We need a standalone member sign-in application — the front
door for all future member-facing journeys — so that a member can
authenticate themselves online with their member ID and a password, and
downstream portals can trust that authentication.

## Background and current state

- There is no member-facing authentication capability today; portals under
  construction (claims, retirement) each assume "an authenticated member"
  and none provides authentication itself.
- The service desk performs manual identity verification by phone, which
  adds handling time to every member interaction and cannot scale to the
  online claim submission volumes forecast for next year.
- This is deliberately a new, separate application: authentication must be
  a shared front door, not a feature copied into each portal.

## Requirements

1. A member can sign in with their member ID and password on a single,
   clearly branded MapleSure sign-in page.
2. Credentials are validated against the member credential store; a
   successful sign-in shows a signed-in landing view confirming the
   member's display name and last sign-in time.
3. A failed sign-in shows one generic error message — it must not reveal
   whether the member ID or the password was wrong.
4. After five consecutive failed attempts for the same member ID, the
   account is temporarily locked for fifteen minutes and the page says so
   without revealing whether the credentials were otherwise correct.
5. A "Forgotten your password?" link is present and routes to a placeholder
   contact-the-service-desk page (self-serve reset is out of scope for this
   release).
6. Every sign-in attempt (success, failure, lockout) is recorded in an
   audit log with member ID, timestamp and outcome — never the password.
7. The sign-in form is keyboard-accessible, labels every field, and meets
   WCAG AA contrast on the MapleSure palette.
8. Passwords are never stored or logged in plain text; the credential store
   holds salted hashes only.

## Out of scope

- Self-serve password reset, multi-factor authentication, and federation
  with employer identity providers (future phases).
- Member registration/enrolment — credential records are provisioned by
  the existing membership back office.

## Success measures

- A member with valid credentials reaches the signed-in landing view in
  one attempt.
- Invalid attempts never disclose which credential was wrong.
- Lockout engages on the fifth consecutive failure and releases after
  fifteen minutes.
- Zero passwords in any log or audit record.

## Notes for delivery

Keep the application small and self-contained: one sign-in page, one
signed-in landing view, one placeholder help page, a credential store with
salted hashes, and the audit log. Synthetic member data only.

transcript.text:
What system will act as the 'member credential store' for authentication?
Will the audit log need to integrate with any existing logging or monitoring infrastructure?

Q: What system will act as the 'member credential store' for authentication?
A: The credential store is a new SQLite table inside this application, provisioned by the membership back office via a nightly synthetic feed — salted hashes only, no external identity system in this phase.
Q: Will the audit log need to integrate with any existing logging or monitoring infrastructure?
A: No external integration this phase: the audit log is an append-only table inside the application; the operations team reads it via a read-only report page later.
What technology stack will be used for developing the MapleSure Member Sign-In application?

Q: What technology stack will be used for developing the MapleSure Member Sign-In application?
A: Flask + SQLite — a small self-contained Python web application; repository name maplesure-member-signin

# README for maplesure-member-signin

## Introduction
The `maplesure-member-signin` application is intended to provide secure and efficient sign-in functionality for MapleSure members using their designated member ID and password.

## Technology Stack
- **Framework**: Flask
- **Database**: SQLite

## Current State
This is a new application with no code or functionality developed as of yet.

## Usage
Once implemented, this application will allow MapleSure members to sign in using their member ID and password.

# Architecture Documentation for maplesure-member-signin

## Overview
The `maplesure-member-signin` application is a standalone application designed to facilitate sign-in for MapleSure members using their member ID and password.

## Stack
- **Framework**: Flask
- **Database**: SQLite

## Components
Currently, there are no components built for this application.

## Data
At this point, there is no data available or stored within this application.

## What this application does NOT do
- This application does not currently have any code or implemented features. It is a new application, and development has not yet started.

stories.title: Implement Sign-In Page with Accessibility and Branding
stories.purpose: Create the UI for a member sign-in page that meets accessibility standards and MapleSure branding guidelines.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given the sign-in page, when viewed on any device, then it should display with MapleSure branding including logo and colors.
Given the sign-in page, when navigating via keyboard only, then all fields should be focusable and interactable.
Given the sign-in page, when viewed, then all text must meet WCAG AA contrast requirements.

rollback_plan.method: Revert UI commit in the repository.

stories.title: Implement Credential Validation and Error Handling
stories.purpose: Build back-end logic for validating member credentials against the in-application SQLite database, handling successful and failed sign-in attempts.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a member ID and password, when valid, then the system shows a landing page with the member's display name and last sign-in time.
Given incorrect credentials, when a member attempts to sign in, then the system displays a generic error message.
Given five consecutive failed attempts for a member ID, when attempts continue, then the account is temporarily locked, showing a notification.

stories.title: Establish Audit Logging for Sign-In Attempts
stories.purpose: Create an audit log that records every sign-in attempt, capturing the required details for monitoring and accountability.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given any sign-in attempt, when it occurs, then it is recorded in the audit log with member ID, timestamp, and outcome.
Given a member sign-in attempt, when recorded, then the password is never stored.

rollback_plan.method: Drop audit log table from the database.

stories.title: Build Password Reset Link and Handling
stories.purpose: Integrate a 'Forgotten your password?' feature that routes to a placeholder service desk contact page for member support.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given the sign-in page, when the 'Forgotten your password?' link is clicked, then it routes the user to a contact-the-service-desk page.
Given a routable URL, when accessed, then it shows the placeholder 'Contact Service Desk' page with instructions.

rollback_plan.method: Remove password reset link from UI.
